text:
jia: Heads-up: small but noisy incident in eu-west3 around 03:40 UTC. A single rack (rack-7) showed sustained PCIe errors and NIC resets, allocator drained 4 hosts, a couple of dedicated slices were affected. Not full outage but noticeable p99 bump and cost regen.

noah: Do we have a root cause signal? PCIe errors could be firmware, or thermal-induced link retries. Any correlation with recent maintenance?

jia: No maintenance. Kernel logs from node-gpu-71 show: `pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 00e0` plus `mlx5_core: link down`. Seems like a local host hardware fault triggering allocator health pathway.

sam: For mitigation I did two quick things: 1) set allocator to prefer host-avoid for dedicated slices rather than immediate preemptive-drain for 30m, 2) adjusted routing so shared low-priority tenants can absorb spill before touching reserved pools. Command: 
```
./ctl allocator set-preempt-mode --mode avoid-first --ttl 1800 --by=operator:sam
```

infra-bot: policy-change applied id=pcie-avoid-1787654321 by sam; change=avoid-first preempt-mode TTL 1800s.

kai: Long-term: we should add a PCIe AER signal into the health aggregator and weight it differently than a heartbeat miss. Right now a single AER -> unhealthy -> drain is too aggressive. Proposal: require either 2 distinct error classes (AER + NIC link) OR persistent error window of 30s before evacuation.

noah: Agreed. Also let's add a targeted metric to cost dashboard: "spill-regen-cost by tenant" so we can see when KV-cache warmups drive billing spikes.

jia: I'll open a follow-up ticket with timeline and attach kernel logs. For the immediate postmortem: action items we agreed: 1) revert aggressive preemptive-drain triggers -> add AER debounce (kai) 2) keep dedicated-safety preference for 1h (sam) 3) hardware ticket for rack-7 (oncall) 4) dashboard tile for spill regen costs (noah).

oncall: HW team acknowledged, they will inspect rack-7 tomorrow morning local time. If we see recurrence escalate to incident.

kai: For the debounce change I'll PR a small allocator tweak: require either (heartbeat_miss >=2) OR (AER_count >=2 within 1m) before mark_unhealthy. Sending PR link in thread when ready.

sam: Thx. Also can ops set a temporary placement rule to avoid co-locating heavy batch tenants with low-latency tenants on same host? That reduces PCIe contention risk.

ja: Good call. I'll add "anti-affinity heavy-batch" to pool templates and roll it to eu-west3 as an experiment.

jia: Closing note: no customer SLA breaches detected, just elevated p99 and cost wobble. Keeping thread open 24h for recurrence updates.
